Disposal of Domestic and Solid Wastes
Production of waste waters and solid wastes from a conversion plant would require that ample land acreage be set aside for disposal. In addition, a population influx due to the conversion plant would require that new and/or renovated domestic sewage treatment plant facilities be provided in the affected communities, since strict new Federal and State water pollution control standards would be applicable.
Should waste water treatment facilities prove inadequate to handle plant and population wastes, the resultant impact upon the environment could be severe. Discharge of untreated or poorly treated sewage into natural water courses could exceed the natural purification capacity of nearby streams and rivers (depending upon the particular set of conditions present). If this occurred, drastic changes in the chacteristics of aquatic life could result. However, the likelihood of this occurrence should be remote since Federal and State water pollution control standards would be imposed.
Solid wastes from energy conversion would be disposed of in sanitary landfills or other approved disposal facilities in compliance with Federal and State standards.
